title: Jill Newhouse Gallery presents Gerard Mossé: Light Rising: Watercolors 1998-2000
summary: Jill Newhouse Gallery is pleased to have on view their third show of works by New York artist Gerard Mossé. These 21 vibrant watercolors were done from 1998-2000, at the end of a period of transition and struggle in the artist’s life, and represent the beginning of his career commitment to the depiction of light through color. Paul Klee, experiencing the distinct quality of light in North Africa during a visit to Tunisia, once quipped, “Color possesses me. I don’t have to pursue it. It will possess me always... Color and I are one. I am a painter.” It is an apt quote for the series of watercolors Gerard Mossé on view at Jill Newhouse Gallery. Born in Casablanca, Morocco, Gerard Mossé moved to Marseille at age 12 and later to Los Angeles. title: Masterpiece Klimt landscape headlining Christie's 20th Century Evening Sale
summary: Christie's New York announced that Litzlbergkeller, one of Gustav Klimt's finest landscape paintings, will lead New York's 20/21 Fall Marquee Week. The masterpiece will be in the premier auction of the season, the 20th Century Evening Sale, taking place on November 17, just days after the highly anticipated reopening of the Neue Galerie. In the same private collection for nearly three decades, Litzlbergkeller previously set a world record for Klimt when last at auction in May 1997 in the estate sale of Neue Galerie co-founder Serge Sabarasky. The work will be on view at Christie's Hong Kong from October 27-29 prior to exhibition at Rockefeller Center from November 7. title: Rare Jean Royère "Œuf" desk discovered in a cellar to headline Paris design auction
summary: A rare desk by French designer Jean Royère, discovered last summer in the depths of a cellar and believed to be the only recorded example of its kind, will take center stage at an upcoming twentieth-century decorative arts auction organized by Gros & Delettrez in Paris. Created in 1951, the remarkable "Œuf" desk has emerged from decades of obscurity with its original blue velvet upholstery, floral textile backing and metal identification plaque still intact. Estimated at €30,000 to €50,000, the rediscovery offers collectors an opportunity to acquire an exceptionally unusual example of Royère's inventive approach to modern furniture. The desk was initially identified by specialists at the auction house through a photograph taken in the dim light of the cellar where it had been stored. title: Thaddaeus Ropac Paris Marais presents Jordan Casteel's European debut exhibition
summary: Thaddaeus Ropac Paris Marais presents Winter Sun, an exhibition of new paintings by American artist Jordan Casteel, marking her first exhibition in France, as well as the most significant showing of her work in Europe to date. Created in the first half of 2026, the artist situates her paintings in a cool, earthy palette inspired by the light in the depths of winter. Winter Sun reflects on a period of dormancy and renewal, hope and grief, love and loss, and light and darkness. Figurative portraits, landscapes and botanical works deepen Casteel's ongoing observation of kinship, place and transition. Casteel's practice is rooted in the monumentalisation of the collective, offering intimate, dignified encounters that reflect her deep commitment to community. Her subjects – who are always a direct reflection of her surroundings – often bring into focus people of colour as a way of mapping and honouring the social landscape

title: Unique collection of historic Anglo-Indian artworks gifted to Tate by Charles Greig
summary: Tate has received an outstanding collection of 50 artworks by artists who lived and worked in India during the 18th and 19th centuries. Gifted outright and without the use of tax incentives, this generous donation by Charles Greig, a leading art historian and scholar of British India, is an entirely philanthropic act, made with the desire to ensure these masterworks can be accessed and enjoyed by the nation. This remarkable collection will enable Tate to tell rich new stories about the art, people and culture of India during the period of profound cultural , social and political change brought about by Brit ish colonialism in South Asia. Built with great care over four decades, Greig’s collection comprises oil paintings, watercolours and miniatures, which reveal the networks of artists and patrons that shaped the visual culture of 18th and 19th century South Asia. title: Philippe Parreno's Riverrun will receive its world premiere at the 21st Rome Film Festival
summary: Riverrun is a portrait that turns into a landscape. Lucy H is overwhelmed; her psychiatrist, Dr Cruz, sends her to a remote clinic in Spain for observation. A chance encounter with Tony upends her sense of self, setting her on a journey beyond treatment and towards unfamiliar realms of existence. Philippe Parreno’s Riverrun will receive its world premiere at the 21st Rome Film Festival on 24 October 2026 in the Freestyle Section. Starring an international cast led by Charlotte Gainsbourg, with Zoë Saldaña, Vicky Krieps and Angela Molina, Riverrun is an intense and visionary journey exploring the fragility of the body and identity, transformation, and the search for the self. The film will be released in Italy in spring 2027 by Filmclub Distribuzione and Minerva Pictures. title: Mattress Factory unveils Akea Brionne's monumental installation 'Home Is Not A Place'
summary: Mattress Factory presents Home Is Not A Place (2026) by Akea Brionne. Known for her figurative, wall-based work, Brionne takes a significant step into architectural-scale installation, using textile, structure, and place to deepen our understanding of permanence and home. "I was eight years old when Hurricane Katrina hit New Orleans. It was my first true understanding that the concept of home could disappear. As Louisiana continues to lose land, I find myself reckoning with the possibility that my home could one day become a myth, like Atlantis. What unsettles me about Atlantis is that we no longer know whether it was ever there. Its existence is contested; a place has become a story, passed down through generations, suspended somewhere between history and myth. title: Lenbachhaus hosts Germany's first major retrospective of Polish modernist Maria Jarema
summary: Maria Jarema (1908–1958) had many talents: A sculptor and painter, she worked with print techniques, designed costumes and stage sets for dance and theater, and was a practicing actress. She published on art, demanded women’s rights to creative and reproductive self-determination, and authored manifestos against class society. Kraków was the center of her life. There, in the early 1930s, she associated with the Kraków Group (Grupa Krakowska) with fellow students, in protest against the nationalist tendencies at the local art academy. The group, which was closely associated with the prohibited Communist Party of Poland (KPP), became an important context for the artistic generation of the interwar and immediate postwar periods. title: From ornate Patek Philippe Calatrava to Cartier Bamboo Coussin, treasured timepieces await at Heritage Auctions
summary: A magnificent timepiece from one of the world’s premier watchmakers, which is as mechanically impressive as it is aesthetically captivating, will get its time in the spotlight as one of the elite offerings in Heritage’s Watches & Fine Timepieces Signature® Auction Nov. 20. The discontinued Patek Philippe Calatrava Rare Handcrafts, Platinum Case, 18k White Gold Engraved Dial, Ref. 5088/100P-001 combines understated design with refined craftsmanship, and it boasts accuracy ensured by an ultra-thin self-winding movement visible through the transparent sapphire case back. The 38mm dial features an elaborate weave of ornate handcrafted vines in an eye-catching design beneath Dauphine hands. “This is an elegant marriage of artistry and precision from one of the world’s elite watchmakers,” says Jim Wolf, Heritage’s Director of Watches & Fine Timepieces. “The combination of artistic precision and mechanical ingenuity make this a coveted

title: Five hundred years of royal jewellery to go on show in landmark exhibition at The King's Gallery
summary: The first exhibition ever to explore 500 years of British royal jewellery will open at The King’s Gallery, Buckingham Palace in June 2027. Royal Jewellery: From Coronations to Keepsakes will bring together more than 300 pieces of jewellery from the 16th century to the present day, around two thirds on display for the first time. Jewellery worn by monarchs from Henry VIII and Charles II to Queen Victoria and Queen Elizabeth II will be shown alongside paintings, designs and documents from the Royal Collection and Royal Archives, revealing powerful stories of politics, diplomacy, identity, faith, grief and love across five centuries. Caroline de Guitaut and Kathryn Jones, co-curators of the exhibition, said, ‘This unprecedented exhibition will bring together some of the most important and spectacular royal jewels in British history, many never exhibited publicly before. title: Hubert Robert's architectural fantasies reveal a world between ruins and imagination
summary: Two monumental paintings completed by French artist Hubert Robert in 1797 offer a glimpse into the imagination of one of the eighteenth century's most celebrated painters of architectural ruins. Presented by Colnaghi, the works bring together classical sculpture, invented landscapes, ancient monuments and unexpected architectural combinations, revealing how Robert transformed his memories of Italy into compositions that explored the passage of time and the relationship between history and imagination. Both paintings, measuring 242 by 242 centimeters, belong to Robert's mature period and were created during a particularly significant chapter of his life, following his imprisonment during the French Revolution and his subsequent return to public service as a curator at the Louvre. title: Mathaf unveils major exhibition on the legacy of the Baghdad Modern Art Group
summary: Qatar Museums opened What Lingers in the Artist Mind: Experiments and Legacies of the Baghdad Modern Art Group, a major exhibition at Mathaf: Arab Museum of Modern Art exploring the history, legacy, and enduring relevance of this pivotal collective. The exhibition will be on view 25 October 2026 through 6 February 2027. Drawing extensively from Mathaf’s internationally renowned collections, the exhibition will bring together paintings, sculptures, sketches, photographs, archival materials, and original research to illuminate one of the Arab world's defining artistic movements, and the group’s lasting influence on generations of artists in Iraq and across the wider region. Organised into 17 thematic sections spanning the 1940s to the present day, What Lingers in the Artist Mind offers new perspectives on how the movement emerged, evolved, and continues to shape artistic discourse. title: Ugo Rondinone debuts first solo exhibition in Japan at Kyoto's historic Kiyomizu-dera Temple
summary: Throughout his career, Ugo Rondinone has approached nature not simply as landscape, but as a psychic and spiritual condition—a space through which to contemplate the body, consciousness and our place within the vastness of space and time. For a new off-site project by Sadie Coles HQ and the artist’s first solo exhibition in Japan, seventeen stone figure sculptures, a sun painting, and a single totemic monk sculpture will be installed at Kiyomizu-dera Temple in Kyoto, one of the most celebrated and historic Buddhist places of worship in the country. Rough-hewn from bluestone, the stone figures draw upon archaic forms, ancient cairns and the enduring human impulse to gather, balance and stack stone. Their elemental silhouettes evoke the inuksuk structures of Arctic Indigenous cultures, while also carrying a deeply personal resonance for Rondinone: his father was a stonemason. title: PHI Foundation presents concurrent exhibitions by Jean-François Bouchard and Stephanie Comilang
summary: With Turn or Burn, Jean-François Bouchard’s first museum-scale exhibition, and ANTHEMS, Stephanie Comilang’s most comprehensive presentation to date and her first exhibition in Québec, PHI presents two perspectives on the narratives, beliefs, and invisible forces that shape our societies. Through distinct approaches—one documentary and installation-based, the other speculative and immersive—the two artists explore systems of belief, collective narratives, and invisible networks that shape the way we understand the world. For his first museum-scale exhibition, Jean-François Bouchard’s Turn or Burn brings together a series of new works that document his encounters with evangelical street preachers in the United States of America. title: Museum of Arts and Design presents John Procario's first solo museum exhibition
summary: Wood bends, light dances, and sculpture becomes something to experience in motion in John Procario: Freeforms—Sculptural Explorations in Wood and Light on view at the Museum of Arts and Design (MAD) from Tuesday, October 27, 2026, through Sunday, April 4, 2027. The first solo museum presentation of Procario’s work, the exhibition features suspended light sculptures, sconces, seating, and freestanding works in which ash wood is bent by hand into open, looping forms and illuminated from within. Procario’s sculptures begin with a material pushed close to its limits. Using a process of freeform bentwood lamination, he bends thin layers of ash wood into curves that are then bonded into permanent forms, often working from no more than a rough sketch. title: Cortesi Gallery showcases a Wunderkammer of rare drawings and photography
summary: Cortesi Gallery presents Il segno e lo sguardo. Featuring a Wunderkammer of Drawings and Photographs from Private Collections, opening on Tuesday, 27 October 2026 at its Milan gallery. Bringing together painting, sculpture, drawing and photography, the exhibition explores how artists transform visual experience into a personal language: the body becomes line, colour becomes rhythm, and matter becomes mark. Through works from different periods and artistic perspectives, the exhibition connects the gesture that generates a form with the gaze that interprets it. title: Emily Ansenk appointed Director of Eye Filmmuseum
summary: Eye's Supervisory Board announced the appointment of Emily Ansenk; her background, experience and personality are all grounds for every confidence in a successful future. Ansenk succeeds Bregtje van der Haak, who left the museum last April. Interim Director John Middelweerd will continue in the role until Ansenk’s arrival. Emily Ansenk’s appointment marks the beginning of a sparkling new period for Eye. The financial forecast for 2026 looks promising, thanks in part to the great success of The Odyssey on 70mm. Eye is the custodian of a unique film collection, as well as an internationally renowned venue that welcomes a wide, diverse audience to discover and celebrate film art and culture in all its myriad forms. title: Apollo 17 astronaut Gene Cernan's handwritten lunar rover repair instructions sell for $510,000 at auction
summary: A wrist-mounted checklist containing Gene Cernan’s handwritten instructions for repairing a damaged lunar rover fender sold for $510,000 in RR Auction’s Space Exploration auction, which closed Oct. 22. Cernan wore the checklist on his left wrist during Apollo 17’s second moonwalk on Dec. 12, 1972. During the mission’s first moonwalk, his spacesuit caught and tore away the lunar rover’s right rear fender. Without it, the rover’s wheels threw lunar dust onto the astronauts, their equipment and cameras. Mission Control developed a repair using spare lunar rover maps, lunar module brackets and gray tape. Cernan recorded the radioed instructions on a blank page at the back of his checklist. He and fellow astronaut Harrison Schmitt made the replacement fender before beginning their second moonwalk. title: Haus Mödrath introduces new three-floor format with trio of Rhineland artists
summary: Haus Mödrath announced a new format in which each of its three floors hosts a different solo show – each in conversation with the others. The first edition welcomes three Rhineland-based artists – Ursula Schulz-Dornburg (b. 1938), Hubert Kiecol (b. 1950), and Behrang Karimi (b.1980) – whose works explicitly engage with their location and its surroundings. Across their three different approaches, media, and generations, one overarching question remains: How can something appear so rich in history that it seems to predate its own creation? Even Haus Mödrath offers interesting answers to this question. Built around 1830, this classicist manor house has changed identities several times over its turbulent history, for example being used as a Nazi training center during World War II, but afterwards also as a children’s home. title: Curran Hatleberg exhibits decade-long photographic study of the American South
summary: Higher Pictures presents River’s Dream 2010-2020 by Curran Hatleberg, the artist’s fourth solo exhibition with the gallery. For the first time, the complete opus of sixty-five photographs is on view. Emerging from the photographer’s sustained presence in the South-Eastern United States, River’s Dream narrates the turbulent and unresolved coexistence of human and non-human life; the encroachment of heat, water, and vegetation on the built environment; economic precarity; and a possibility of connection across political and social differences. Installed together, the photographs allow these themes to accumulate and echo across the gallery walls. An encounter with a reptile in one frame finds its counterpart in a figure at rest in another, while recurring motifs of water, overgrowth, and decay link people, animals, and place into a single ecosystem.

title: Fondazione Biscozzi │ Rimbaud survey brings private Salento collections to Lecce
summary: In the heart of the historic centre of Lecce, Fondazione Biscozzi | Rimbaud carries out a cultural project conceived by Luigi Biscozzi and Dominique Rimbaud, a couple who wished to make their contemporary art collection, gathered over the years, accessible to the public. Founded in 2018, the Foundation includes in its collection artworks by Italian and international artists, with a particular focus on the artistic production from the 1960s to the present. The collection marks the starting point for a programme that combines a permanent exhibition, temporary exhibitions, talks, educational activities, and research and in-depth study projects. The seasonal exhibitions programme officially began in 2021 with an exhibition dedicated to Angelo Savelli. title: Christie's New York presents The William I. Koch Collection
summary: Christie's announced the William I. Koch Collection will headline the 20th/21st Century Art Sales during the November Marquee Week of Sales in New York. The collection features stunning examples by Impressionist masters Claude Monet, Edgar Degas, Auguste Rodin and Paul Cezanne complemented by Modern highlights by Marc Chagall, Henri Matisse, Joan Miro and Diego Rivera, among others. Works will be offered in the premier sale of the week, the 20th Century Evening Sale as well as the Impressionist and Modern Art Day and Works on Paper Sales. In total, the collection is expected to achieve in excess of $40 million. The selection to be offered this November represents a rich cross-section of exemplary artworks by European and Latin American masters. title: A new home for Latino creativity opens its doors in Denver
summary: The Latino Cultural Arts Center (LCAC) will welcome the public to its permanent home at 1935 W. 12th Ave., marking nearly a decade of planning, building and community collaboration. Here, culture takes shape in classrooms, studios, kitchens and gathering spaces. Through exhibitions, performances, arts education and creative career development, LCAC will give artists, young people and families a place to carry traditions forward and develop ideas of their own. The location gives that mission particular resonance. Near Auraria, where urban renewal displaced hundreds of families from a deeply rooted Latino community in the 1960s and 1970s, LCAC established a lasting cultural presence.
